summary: The semicircle risk gauge shown in the event and customer drawers, the Simulation Center and the Lab. The arc is drawn with polar-to-Cartesian maths and an SVG arc command, and one tweened number drives the arc length, the riding knob, the readout and the colour, so the arc visibly changes level as it climbs. `levelOf` from dom.js picks the level, and the `lvl-*` classes from tokens.css supply the colours.

notes.text: Header comment. One animated value drives everything (the arc, the dot riding it, the number and the colour), so as the value climbs the arc changes level from slate to amber to orange to red.
Imports `levelOf` (score to LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL using the 30/60/80 thresholds) from dom.js, and `animate`/`motionEnabled` from motion.js.

Geometry in SVG units (the viewBox is 220 by 124): the centre `CX, CY` is at the horizontal middle near the bottom and `R` is the radius, so the top of the semicircle is at y = 108 − 88 = 20, leaving room above for tick labels.
`point(f)` takes a fraction of the gauge (a score / 100) and turns it into an angle with `θ = π(1 − f)`: 0 maps to 180° (the left end), 0.5 to 90° (the top) and 1 to 0° (the right end).
Polar to Cartesian: `x = CX + R·cos θ` and `y = CY − R·sin θ`. The minus is needed because SVG's y axis points down; subtracting makes the arc bulge upward.
`arc(f0, f1)` builds the path for the part of the semicircle between two fractions, starting from their two end points.

The path moves to the start, then uses the SVG elliptical-arc command `A rx,ry rotation large-arc-flag sweep-flag x,y`: both radii are `R`, rotation 0, large-arc flag 0 (a gauge never spans more than half a circle) and sweep flag 1 (clockwise on screen, so up and over from left to right). `toFixed(2)` keeps the numbers short.
The four zones as fractions of the gauge, matching the engine's thresholds: LOW 0–0.3, MEDIUM 0.3–0.6, HIGH 0.6–0.8, CRITICAL 0.8–1.

`gauge(el, score, options)`: `caption` is the small text under the number, `delay` postpones the animation and `from` is the starting value. The Lab passes the previous score as `from`, so the gauge moves from the old result to the new one instead of from zero.

Builds tick marks at the threshold scores 0, 30, 60, 80 and 100: for each, the point on the arc and the unit vector pointing outward from the centre, `(point − centre) / R`, which has length 1 because every point is exactly R away.

Each tick is a short line from 10 to 16 units outside the arc (just beyond the 14-unit-wide stroke), and its label sits 26 units out, with +3 to centre the text vertically. `join("")` turns the array into one string.
Writes the gauge: a wrapper `div` and an SVG with a fixed `viewBox` (CSS scales it, so no `responsive` is needed) and an `aria-label` that states the score for screen readers.
The track: the whole semicircle in a dark surface colour (charts.css makes it 14 wide with round caps).
The zone bands, each drawn faintly (13% opacity in charts.css) in its own risk colour via its `lvl-` class. Each is trimmed by 0.004 at both ends to leave hairline gaps between zones.
Inserts the tick marks and labels built above.

The value arc covers the whole semicircle, but `pathLength="100"` makes the browser treat its length as exactly 100 units, so `stroke-dasharray="v 100"` paints a dash covering v% of the arc followed by a gap. It starts at `0 100` (nothing visible) with the LOW colour.
The knob: a small circle that rides the end of the value arc, starting at the left end, `point(0)`.
Closes the SVG and adds the readout: an HTML number starting at 0 with the caption below it, which CSS positions at the bottom centre, inside the semicircle.
References to the three elements that change while animating: the value arc, the knob and the number.
`render(v)` draws the gauge for any value from 0 to 100; first it works out the level class for the rounded value, e.g. `lvl-HIGH` for 67.
Sets the dash to v out of 100, so the coloured arc covers v% of the semicircle.
Moves the knob to the point at fraction v / 100, the leading end of the arc.

Only when the level changes, replaces the class on the arc and the knob. Their colour comes from `var(--lvl)`, which the `lvl-` class sets, so crossing 30, 60 or 80 mid-animation switches the colour: this is the level-changing arc. `setAttribute("class", ...)` swaps the whole class list at once, removing the old level.
Shows the rounded value in the readout; the closing brace ends `render`.
A plain object `{ v }` for anime.js to tween (it can animate any numeric property, not just CSS), and an immediate render of the starting value.
With motion off (the reduced-motion setting, the in-app toggle, or a hidden tab) the gauge jumps straight to the final score; `return render(score)` renders and exits in one statement.

Otherwise tweens `state.v` to the score over 1.4 s with the decelerating `outExpo` ease, calling `render` on every frame so the arc, knob, number and colour all move together. The closing brace ends `gauge`.
